analytical_models.equation_role: Determine phase composition at each rolling temperature and the carbide precipitation/dissolution range
analytical_models.model_name: Iron-carbon equilibrium phase diagram and phase-fraction vs temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Carbides fall to zero at ~710 °C; used to justify retained carbide/ferrite composite lamellae at low rolling temperature (R650)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase diagram and phase fractions vs temperature computed for the tested steel composition
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted carbide stability temperature range (<750 °C) consistent with the decreasing carbide/ferrite proportion from 650 °C to 750 °C observed by OM

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: After impact deformation numerous dislocations are blocked by carbides and pile up in regions adjacent to carbides; when carbide diameter exceeds 10 nm numerous dislocations and atomic shearing observed at ferrite/carbide boundaries (Orowan mechanism); carbides (diameter <250 nm) pin dislocations, increasing dislocation density and strain hardening capacity.

Crack tip becomes significantly blunted and stops propagating on penetrating the carbide/ferrite lamellae; interface separation disperses crack-tip stress; spherical carbides act as microvoid nucleation sites at carbide/ferrite interfaces, and secondary defects propagate along the horizontal lamellae direction.

interfaces.interface_notes: The carbide/ferrite composite lamellae bear most of the crack propagation resistance; carbides are concentrated outside δ-ferrite lamellae.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Supersaturated martensite breaks down under large plastic deformation during low-temperature rolling; deformation energy activates diffusion of C, Cr and Mn which enrich at defect sites (dislocations, grain boundaries) and precipitate carbides; new ferrite forms in low-carbon regions near carbides, producing composite lamellae with carbides dispersed in a ferrite matrix.

phase_interfaces.coherence: obvious boundaries exist between the lamellae; boundary nearly free of carbides
bonding force at the carbide/ferrite interface is greater than at the ferrite/ferrite interface; interfacial stress partly transferred to carbides

interfaces.slip_behavior: In δ-ferrite lamellae cracks propagate in plane strain along the lamellar orientation; in carbide/ferrite lamellae the crack front is blunted (plane stress) and forced to deflect/branch along lamellar boundaries.

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: R750 impact absorption energy decreased by approximately 60 % compared with R650

service_conditions.stress_state: impact (Charpy V-notch, plane strain in δ-ferrite; plane stress in carbide/ferrite lamellae) and uniaxial tension along RD

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel ingot (fabricated via VIM) homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h prior to hot forging.
Hot forged to a thickness of 40 mm, then air cooled to room temperature.
Specimens placed in a box furnace and heated to 650 °C and held for 2 h before rolling.
Hot rolling deformation with 60 % reduction ratio, reducing plate thickness from 40 mm to 16 mm.
After rolling, samples were air cooled to room temperature, yielding R650.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Tensile: rod-shaped specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, sampled along RD; Charpy: 10 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm V-notch bar, notch machined on rolled surface, impact direction perpendicular to RD

strain_hardening_rate.value: hump-shaped θ curve; peak near true strain 0.035 at ~2400 (R650)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve (Fig. 5d): long plateau near ~860 MPa with the largest elongation of the four conditions

grain_structure.texture: dominant orientation <001> (low-temperature rolling zone); fine red/purple lamellar banded grains in IPF

phases_present.morphology: lamellae (dark areas, continuous banded); ultra-fine spherical carbides dispersed in ferrite matrix

precipitates.distribution: dispersed as ultra-fine spherical particles in the ferrite matrix of the C/F lamellae; high distribution density 1.7 ± 0.2 μm^-2; mainly concentrated outside the δ-ferrite lamellae; diameter <250 nm
precipitates.type: ultra-fine spherical carbides: MC, M3C, M23C6, M7C3

structures.overall_structure: Lamellar structure with alternating δ-ferrite (δ-F) lamellae (light) and carbide/ferrite (C/F) composite lamellae (dark); both lamellae types show continuous banded distribution parallel to RD. No martensite present.

unmapped_findings: R650 room-temperature impact absorption energy (IAE) = 207.5 ± 29.3 J (Table 4), the highest of the four rolling conditions; abstract/conclusion states the impact energy reaches up to 207.5 J.

R650 crack initiation energy Ei and propagation energy Ep: main text states Ei = 59.6 J and Ep = 147.9 J, whereas the Fig. 5b annotation prints Ei = 92.93 J and Ep = 147.90 J for R650; these two sources disagree.
R650 strength-plasticity product (SPP = Rm × A) = 16.5 ± 1.5 GPa% (Table 4); abstract/text also quote 16.51 GPa·%.
R650 HAGBs = 49.6 %, GOS ≤ 2° = 12.3 %, dislocation density = 3.9 × 10^14 m^-2 (Table 3).
R650 KAM value reported in the range 0.48–0.55° for the low-temperature rolling zone, indicating high dislocation density.
R650 dominant texture orientation is <001> (low-temperature rolling zone), shifting to <101> at high temperature.
R650 nano-hardness: carbide/ferrite composite lamellae 3.64 GPa vs δ-ferrite 2.92–2.93 GPa, hardness difference 0.72 GPa (Table 3 gives C/F 3.6 ± 0.6 GPa, F 2.9 ± 0.3 GPa).
Carbides in the R650 carbide/ferrite lamellae identified by SAED as MC, M3C, M23C6 and M7C3; carbide regions are C- and Mn-rich, weakly Cr-enriched and not Al-enriched (EDS).

Work-hardening rate (θ) curve of R650 is hump-shaped (peak near true strain 0.035 at ~2400), attributed to Orowan pinning of dislocations by carbides (diameter <250 nm); this delays necking and contributes to the strength-plasticity synergy.

Fracture mechanism of R650 is ductile with a mixed-mode pattern: crack blunting resists propagation perpendicular to the lamellae while lamellar separation and microvoids (nucleated at carbides) drive horizontal crack propagation; tensile fracture shows a serrated delamination morphology.
R650 tensile fracture deflection was confined within δ-ferrite lamellae and ran parallel to the lamellar orientation.
